analysis.title: Network Thoughts: Politics Have Taken Over From Macro As The Next New Market Driver
key_insights: After the Democratic midterm sweep, investors face the risk that Congress and new state governments restrain the AI and data-centre boom. In Q2, US GDP grew 2.2% y/y, with AI investment contributing a full percentage point, upper-quartile income consumption a percentage point, and everything else 0.2pp.

Slowing tech growth also threatens the credit funding the build-out. Brookings puts cumulative spending plans at $10.3trn by 2032. The note says the financing, rather than AI itself, could be what pops.
Defensives are not a clean refuge because their earnings growth is typically well below current US real rates of 2.60%. AA-rated non-financial credit trades at 5.5% and BBB at 6%.
Long-end Treasury yields are not obviously set to fall. The Fed is hard pressed to ease with inflation high, and a 6.5% deficit with slowing growth does not support duration demand.

A slowdown in AI data-centre capex could relieve supply shortages, most severely in semi memory. Asian memory semis have given up their Q2 gains and are back at early-April levels, which the note reads as the market pricing a sizable drop in memory prices.

Before the midterms, AI slowdown signals were in the ability to fund and deploy capacity, not in end demand. Incoming Texas and Georgia governors have advocated moratoriums on new data-centre approvals.

UBS Research expects 2027 data-centre build rates to be largely unaffected, because projects are mostly permitted, grid-connected and under construction. 'Bring your own power', grid-funding and water rules could raise demand for power equipment and grid investment even if MW deployment slows.
UBS Technology Research projects cloud sales growth accelerating from 64% in 2026 to 97% in 2027. Cloud backlog is about 3.5x forward 12-month sales and US data-centre vacancy is below 2%.
UBS bottom-up forecasts require 393GW of data-centre capacity by 2030. 45GW is under construction and 231GW planned, leaving 117GW of projects still required.

Hyperscaler top-6 ROIC has moderated from 20-25% to 16-18% in 2026-27, above a 10-11% WACC. The funding constraint is that top-13 hyperscaler 2027 capex is forecast at $1.77trn (+70%), against $1.47trn of operating cash flow, a gap of about $300bn.

On Thursday, 85% of SPX constituents fell and the index dropped 4.7%, the sharpest re-correlation of US stocks since Q1. VIX rose almost 12pts close-to-close to 29, the largest increase since the April 2025 tariff announcement, with record S&P put activity and one of the busiest VIX call sessions in years.

NDX fell 6.4%, its largest decline ever from a starting VIX below 20. SOXX fell 12.2%, its second largest decline in 25 years behind March 16, 2020. The 3x long SOXL fund fell 39% and is down 75% from early October despite record inflows.

0DTE investors have generally bought the dip, while broader retail flipped to selling (RMM flows at the 1st percentile Thursday). UBS strategists' SPX year-end target of 8100 implies over 10% upside, with Q3 EPS growth of 31.6%.

UBS flags the SPX 31Dec26 7800/8100 call spread at 36pts / 49bps indicative (vs 7365.3 spot reference) as a defensive recovery position, returning over 7x on premium if 8100 is reached. The spread trades on under 15 vol, versus VIXEQ near 50.

UBS forecasts October US CPI at 26bp versus 29bp consensus, with September at 59bp. Core is 23bp (UBS) versus 24bp (consensus), against 37bp in September, driven by a projected 1.5% fall in used-car prices. Year-over-year figures will not be published because October 2025 data is unavailable due to the government shutdown.

The December FOMC stub traded as low as 16bp on Nov 5, cutting the implied hike probability from roughly 80% to 60% during the equity selloff. After the hotter nonfarm payrolls report it gapped back to 20bp.

Hedge funds and asset managers were bearish USD before the midterms (net cumulative flows -1.5σ and -2.9σ). The equity selloff produced a safe-haven USD bid that persisted after payrolls beat at 165k vs 70k estimated, with unemployment at 4.1%. The bid is stronger in G10 than EMFX: NOK -240bp, AUD -200bp, NZD -139bp since Oct 30.

China tech has shifted from laggard to relative outperformer. Beijing announced liquidity support Monday, and unwinding of the crowded memory long reduced the hedge fund pair trade's short leg in Hong Kong and China, so short covering lifted China tech.

The Bank of England hiked Bank Rate 25bp to 4.00% and is likely to hike again. UK inflation is 3.5% and the bank fears nearly 5% by mid-2027, mostly from the Iran war and energy prices. Household energy and motor fuel account for about 60% of the overshoot versus the 2% target.

UBS considers market pricing of a cumulative 75bp of BoE hikes by September 2027 unnecessarily pessimistic, and sees Gilt yields as likely lower given weak growth (BoE forecasts 1.3% GDP next year) and fiscal challenges.

sector_views.rationale: Rotating into defensives does not help because their earnings growth is typically well below current US real rates of 2.60%.
Politics and funding can slow AI deployment but not hold back the tide. 2027 build is largely secured, while funding and post-2027 capacity are the open questions.
Policy support and short covering from the memory-trade unwind turned China tech into a relative winner. Fundamentals have changed little.

tension_points.theme: AI data-centre buildout under political pressure
tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees 2027 build rates largely unaffected because projects are permitted, grid-connected and under construction. Cloud sales growth is projected to accelerate from 64% to 97%, backlog is about 3.5x forward sales, vacancy is below 2%, and top-6 hyperscaler ROIC of 16-18% exceeds a 10-11% WACC.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic officials and incoming Texas and Georgia governors may curb approvals. The top-13 hyperscalers face a funding gap of about $300bn in 2027, and 117GW of the capacity needed by 2030 is not yet planned.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A policy halt on new data-centre development, rather than a 'bring your own power' framing, or credit conditions tightening enough to stop the capex funding.

tension_points.bear_case: The Fed is hard pressed to ease with high inflation, and a 6.5% deficit against dwindling growth does not support duration appetite.
